tip.title: depuis & plaire
tip.body: To say how long you have been doing something that is still going on, French uses the present + depuis: Je travaille ici depuis deux ans (I've been working here for two years). plaire works 'backwards', like 'to please': Mon travail me plaît (my job pleases me = I like my job). Linking: in huit heures the t runs straight into heures — 'hui-teur' — and in je finis the final s is silent.

tip.title: me, te, vous before the verb
tip.body: Small object pronouns go before the verb in French: Tu peux m'aider ? (can you help me?), Je t'envoie le fichier (I'm sending you the file). me and te shorten to m' and t' before a vowel. With your boss or a client, Pourriez-vous … ? is extra polite. In pourriez-vous, the -ez is said like 'ay' and the s of vous is silent.

tip.title: No article with jobs
tip.body: After être, jobs take no article: Je suis infirmière, Il est comptable. With c'est you need one: C'est une infirmière. Many jobs have a feminine form: infirmier → infirmière, vendeur → vendeuse, directeur → directrice. In infirmier the final r is silent ('in-fir-myé'); in infirmière you hear it.

lessons.title: -ir, -re and irregular verbs
lessons.goal: Use finir, attendre, faire, prendre and venir in the present.

tip.title: finir, attendre, faire, prendre, venir
tip.body: -ir verbs like finir add -iss- in the plural: je finis, tu finis, il finit, nous finissons, vous finissez, ils finissent. -re verbs like attendre: j'attends, tu attends, il attend, nous attendons, vous attendez, ils attendent. Three key irregulars: faire (je fais, nous faisons, vous faites, ils font), prendre (je prends, nous prenons, ils prennent), venir (je viens, nous venons, ils viennent). Good news: je, tu, il forms usually sound identical. In ils prennent and ils viennent the double n kills the nasal sound: 'prèn', 'vyèn'. In nous faisons, fai- sounds like 'fe'.

story.title: A new colleague
story.intro: In the company canteen, Léa asks her new colleague Thomas about his first month.

lines.name: Léa
lines.t: Salut Thomas ! Alors, comment s'est passé ton premier mois dans l'entreprise ?
lines.n: Hi Thomas! So, how was your first month at the company?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Très bien ! Les collègues sont très sympas, mais je suis débordé.
lines.n: Very good! The colleagues are really nice, but I'm swamped.

lines.name: Léa
lines.t: Tu fais du télétravail, toi aussi ?
lines.n: Do you work from home too?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Oui, le vendredi. Comme ça, je ne prends pas le train.
lines.n: Yes, on Fridays. That way I don't take the train.

lines.name: Léa
lines.t: Et les autres jours, tu viens comment ?
lines.n: And how do you come in on the other days?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: En train, et puis je finis à pied. Ça prend une heure.
lines.n: By train, and then I walk the last bit. It takes an hour.

lines.name: Léa
lines.t: Et le soir, tu pars à quelle heure ?
lines.n: And in the evening, what time do you leave?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: En général, vers dix-sept heures. Mais aujourd'hui, je reste tard : j'ai une réunion avec un client canadien.
lines.n: Usually around five. But today I'm staying late: I have a meeting with a Canadian client.

lines.name: Léa
lines.t: Bon courage ! On mange ensemble demain ?
lines.n: Good luck! Shall we have lunch together tomorrow?

lines.name: Thomas
lines.t: Avec plaisir ! À demain.
lines.n: With pleasure! See you tomorrow.

lessons.title: Talk about your job

culture.title: 35 hours, holidays and vous at work
culture.body: In France the legal working week has been 35 hours since the early 2000s. Many full-time employees work more and get extra days off in return, called RTT. Employees are entitled to five weeks of paid holiday (congés payés) a year, and many take a long break in summer. At work, vous is the safe start with managers, clients and older colleagues; in many offices colleagues soon ask On se tutoie ? — wait for that. In Québec, tutoiement is much more common at work, often even with the boss, and an email is usually un courriel. In Switzerland, working weeks are usually longer than in France, often around 40 hours or more.
